## Leading theory

The best current q13 generator is:

```text
page-level illustrated system
  -> local graphical labels through a section-specialized renderer
  -> an independent sequence of physical prose paragraphs
  -> each paragraph contains HPR2 fields separated by DY or line end
  -> a sparse minority of complete rendered groups can be reused across the
     graphical and prose channels
  -> content values remain unresolved and need not reside in PAGE_HOST alone
```

This is a hybrid **diagram legend plus paragraph-record** architecture.  It is
not a per-figure recipe list: f80r has 10 labels but five prose paragraphs,

## Why this world leads

## Translation consequence

The next real translation gain requires one source-bound referent whose value

what_does_not_follow: The count mismatch does not show that figures cannot have names, that prose cannot contain named records, or that labels never recur across channels.
Sparse exact reuse and failed folio transfer do not establish a universal absence of label dictionaries; they limit this tested simple dictionary/world.
A graphical label can remain a renderer or legend key without being a figure name, and a prose paragraph can remain an independent record without one figure owner.
changed_input_reopen_gate: Reconsider the one-to-one named-record world only after a new, source-bound repeated layout supplies author-visible singular ownership links and a stable label-to-record assignment whose counts and paragraph boundaries are independently matched. Aggregate label/paragraph count equality, proximity, filler mining, or PAGE_HOST recurrence is insufficient. Even then, the result would establish an ownership/record relation before any name or prose meaning.
